record.title: A review on clinical utility of haemato-biochemical biomarkers for assessing severity of Babesia gibsoni infection in dogs
record.journal: International Journal of Advanced Biochemistry Research
record.abstract: The incidence of Babesia gibsoni infections is increasing worldwide, expanding beyond endemic regions into non-endemic regions. The clinical manifestation associated with B. gibsoni infection presents a spectrum ranging from subclinical or asymptomatic symptoms to severe multiorgan dysfunction and death. As of now, specific anti-babesial drug effective against B. gibsoni is unavailable and clinical relapses are frequently observed. Biomarkers are helpful for evaluating organ involvement, quantifying disease severity, measuring therapeutic response, and monitoring disease progression. The application of biomarkers has emerged as an increasing trend in the veterinary practice and being employed in the assessment of diverse health-related parameters such as disease diagnosis, forecasting treatment outcomes, monitoring therapeutic responses and assessing organ dysfunction. There is imperative need to identify clinically relevant and financially sustainable biomarkers among standard haematological and biochemical parameters that support timely detection of single or multiple organ system involvement in veterinary patients.

screening.rationale: Review of haemato-biochemical biomarkers for severity, organ involvement and outcome in B. gibsoni infection.
